summary.name: List of wiki software
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia list cataloguing wiki software programs grouped by use case (standard, personal, hosted-only, wiki-based CMS and project management) and by implementation language.
use_cases: choosing a wiki engine for a team or company
finding a self-hosted wiki to run
setting up a personal note-taking wiki
comparing wiki platforms by programming language
finding enterprise wiki or knowledge management tools
finding wiki features inside project management tools
summary.what_it_does: This Wikipedia list catalogues wiki software programs, grouped into standard wiki engines, personal wiki apps, hosted-only wikis, and content management or project management tools with wiki functionality. Standard engines are further sorted by implementation language (JavaScript, Java, Perl, PHP, Python, Ruby and others). Each entry gives a short description, such as storage model (plain text files, git, single HTML file), licensing, or whether it is commercial or discontinued. The personal section lists apps like Obsidian, Joplin, Zim, Vimwiki and OneNote. The page is a directory rather than a tool, so it does not itself offer features. It is marked as needing more citations.
notable: Organized by use case and by programming language
Covers standard, personal, hosted-only and wiki-enabled CMS/project tools
Notes discontinued or commercial products such as FlexWiki and ConnectedText
caveats: Page is a list, not a single product; it does not verify current availability of each entry
Marked by Wikipedia as needing more citations
Some listed products (e.g. FlexWiki, ConnectedText, Journler) are described as discontinued or no longer available
